limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings between 45,230 and 812,670: 90% of the 2400 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.

applicants with months_unemployed equal to 0: 52% of the 1469 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (1928 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 17,872 against 37,801; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: age p=0.0507 (-883, -684, -854, -1830 dollars per SD); prior_earnings p=0.159 (+1009, +1885, +606, +5864 dollars per SD); education p=0.193 (+868, +387, +949, +127 dollars per SD); region p=0.209 (-1517, -922, -1626, -1949 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
20.6% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 3,986 dollars.
Instrument check (distance_km, responders only): complier effect 4,789 dollars with 90% interval [-1,952, 11,530], against the ATE 5,575. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,673.0 (train) against 25,883.7 (test); months_unemployed 2.7 (train) against 3.2 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 6.9%. 267 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 6,593 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 5.2%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['age', 'prior_earnings', 'education'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
